newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 13.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 13:

DENVER, COLORADO - Timothy McVeigh was so determined to blow up the federal building in Oklahoma City that he considered driving the truck packed with explosives through the front door on a suicide mission, a former Army buddy told jurors.

RICHMOND, VIRGINIA - A Republican plan to eliminate Virginia's personal property tax is based on unlikely economic assumptions and probably could not be implemented without significant cuts in state spending, according to aides to Gov. George Allen.

SAN JUAN ISLANDS, WASHINGTON - Residents on the San Juan Islands have the highest ratio of electric cars to regularly powered vehicles in the country, but in practice, half of those cars are awaiting repairs, remain parked in garages, or sport "For Sale" signs.

WASHINGTON - The FBI has concluded that John Huang, the man at the center of the Democratic Party's fundraising scandal, may be more valuable as a government witness in building a case against White House and DNC officials.
MIAMI - A 22-year-old Australian woman battled through choppy seas and jellyfish stings to become the first person to swim the 105 miles across the Florida Straits from Cuba to the United States.
NEW YORK - The three stars of NBC's hit sitcom "Seinfeld" will be paid $600,000 each per episode under a new contract in which they agreed to continue doing the show for at least the next two years.
